title: Decision Trees & Random Forests from Scratch
summary: Implement Gini and entropy, an exhaustive best-split search by information gain, a recursive decision tree with depth and size limits, and a seeded bagged forest that predicts by majority vote.

ShapeMismatch.hint: Index rows with a boolean mask over X[:, j], not over X. Print the shapes of X[left] and y[left]: they must have the same number of rows.

hints.test_impurity_known_values: Get class proportions with np.unique(y, return_counts=True). Gini = 1 − Σp², entropy = −Σp·log2(p). Return 0.0 for an empty array.
hints.test_best_split_simple_threshold: Candidate thresholds are midpoints between consecutive sorted unique values, e.g. 2.5 between 2 and 3.
hints.test_best_split_matches_brute_force: Loop over every feature and every midpoint; gain = H(parent) − (n_L/n)·H(left) − (n_R/n)·H(right). Keep the first strictly better gain.
hints.test_best_split_weights_children_by_size: Weight each child's impurity by its share of rows, n_child / n. A plain average lets a tiny pure child win.
hints.test_best_split_no_valid_split: Return None when no threshold exists (one unique value per feature) or no split has positive gain (e.g. a pure node).
hints.test_tree_fits_training_data: Recurse until a node is pure (best_split returns None). Return self from fit, and copy rather than modify the input arrays.
hints.test_tree_respects_stopping_rules: Make a leaf when depth >= max_depth, when len(y) < min_samples_split, or when there's no split. Track the deepest node in self.depth_. np.bincount(y).argmax() breaks ties towards the smallest label.
hints.test_threshold_ties_go_left: Use the same rule in fit and predict: go left when x[feature] <= threshold.
hints.test_forest_bootstrap_is_seeded: bootstrap_sample is rng.integers(0, n, size=n). In fit, make one rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) and draw one sample per tree, in order.
hints.test_forest_predicts_majority_vote: Stack every tree's predictions into (n_trees, m) and take the most common label in each column, with ties going to the smallest label.
